answer: Monero has blocked double-spends since 2014, never naming the spender. Each ballot signs in a ring of sixteen — one real, fifteen decoys — and publishes a key image, I = x·Hp(P), a tag of its key, never repeatable. One hand minting 10,000 ballots off a single key publishes one image 10,000 times; the ledger kills copy two on sight, and all 10,000 lose their $25 bonds, $250,000 gone. Fresh keys cost 10,000 devices, 5,000 hours, $500,000. Like an orchard fed by one karst river through one inlet, one key behind many ballots is one river, and a copied image kills 10,000 ballots and $250,000.
